finding: STOP -- the frozen Stage-4A seed protocol gives A0-A3 FOUR DIFFERENT candidate-generation seeds, so physical trace sharing is not available under the protocol as frozen
question_asked: does the benchmark derive the candidate-generation seed from the full METHOD_ID, a shared seed_identity, or something else?

mechanism.consequence: seed_identity falls back to the METHOD_ID itself for every AutoClust arm

frozen_protocol_evidence.reading: Stage 4A deliberately froze AutoClust as PER-ARM seed identity; only the two ClustOpt pairs are listed as sharing a trace

prior_300_config_harness.seed_used: derive_seed(dataset_id, view_id, "IDB_AutoClust_A0") -- ONE seed passed for all four arms
prior_300_config_harness.additional_defect: the literal "IDB_AutoClust_A0" is not even a registry METHOD_ID; the real id is IDB_AutoClust_A0_original_cvis
prior_300_config_harness.what_it_actually_proved: the sampler is a deterministic function of its seed -- identical seed gives an identical configuration list
prior_300_config_harness.what_it_did_NOT_prove: that the frozen benchmark supplies the same seed to A0-A3. It does not.

decision_required_from_project_lead: OPTION 1 -- accept four separate physical AutoClust traces per dataset/view, consistent with the frozen autoclust_per_arm protocol. No protocol change; ~4x candidate execution cost for AutoClust.

OPTION 2 -- a formal PRE-RUN protocol amendment adding an autoclust shared seed identity to TRACE_IDENTITY and trace_reuse.shared, mirroring the ClustOpt C0/C3 and C1/C4 groups. Scientifically defensible because candidate generation was proven independent of the CVI inventory, but it IS a change to a frozen protocol and must be authorised, dated and recorded before any external run.
